description: The account `subtype` repertoire is CLOSED (format 0.9). THE DEFECT IT ENDS is not a wrong figure but an inert one: `subtype` is the field through which the chart tells the engine what an account IS — which movement is profit-neutral, which account is a tax account and on which side its tax stands, which posting opens a receivable — and it was a free string. A pack that wrote `tax-out` instead of `tax_out` produced an account that LOOKED annotated and behaved like an unannotated one: the VAT return skipped it, the cash-basis projection did not treat it as tax, and nothing anywhere said a tax account had gone missing. This is the third time the project has met that shape and answered it the same way — the tax mechanisms were closed in v0.8.0 after `reverse-charge` fell back to plain VAT under the ordinary reporting key, and `PartnerKind` was closed after `custommer` turned out to be a partner kind like any other. TWO ENFORCEMENT POINTS, and they are the two places a subtype is AUTHORED: a pack fails at resolution (`E_PACK_INCOHERENT`, like every other coherence check, so a composed pack fails at `resolvePack` and not at the first posting), and the runtime chart API fails at the call (`E_INPUT_INVALID`, or `E_COA_FORMAT_INVALID` inside an import, whose contract is that a row is refused with its index). WHERE IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT ENFORCED, and this is the reason the check does not sit in the `Account` constructor where it would be shortest: hydrating a stored account runs through that same constructor, so a database written before this repertoire existed would stop loading. A validation that refuses to read back what it once wrote is a worse failure than the one it prevents. THE REPERTOIRE HAS TWO TIERS AND ONE LIST: eight values the engine reads and branches on, plus `fixed_asset`, `opening_balance` and `private`, which are annotation that every shipped pack carries and no code consults — they are in the list because the packs use them, and a repertoire holding only the eight would refuse all three shipped charts.

expect.comment: One character, and before this the pack resolved cleanly: account 177 entered the chart with a subtype nothing reads, so the tenant had no output-tax account and its VAT return quietly reported nothing on it. The refusal names the account and the value, because `unknown subtype` without either is a message that sends the reader to grep.

The same chart with the canonical value resolves exactly as it always did. The repertoire refuses what is unknown and changes nothing about what is known — every account here would have been accepted before format 0.9 too.

THE OTHER AUTHORING BOUNDARY, and the one an embedding application actually touches. A pack is written once and reviewed; accounts are added by users, from a form, at a keyboard. A hyphen for an underscore used to create a liability account that no VAT return would ever count, and the user had no way to find out short of comparing the return against the ledger.
Corrected, and the same number is free — the refusal above created nothing. An account refused for its subtype must not leave its number taken, or the correction would collide with the mistake.
Absent is not unknown. Most accounts in most charts carry no subtype at all, and the repertoire has nothing to say about them.

An import is atomic and refuses the whole batch by row, which is its own contract (E_COA_FORMAT_INVALID, not E_INPUT_INVALID) — so the doubled letter in row 1 also stops row 0 from being created. That is the behaviour an import needs: half a chart of accounts is worse than none.
And the corrected batch goes through whole, which proves the refusal above rolled back rather than half-applied.

What survived: the pack's four, the two accounts created by hand, and the two imported ones. Nothing carries a subtype outside the repertoire, which is the whole claim — and 178 appears exactly once, though it was asked for twice.
